classification_rationale: The /bill/listXml endpoint accepts a status filter (status=3 Delinquent, status=0 Unpaid, status=7 Relevied) and returns a paginated grid of bills county-wide WITHOUT requiring a parcel pre-selection. A single authenticated POST yields 2,084 currently-delinquent bills with parcel SBL, owner name, bill type, base/interest/penalty/amount-due, and bill date — every field needed to originate a tax-distress lead. The optional /bill/show/id/{N} detail view enriches each row with mailing address and explicit Date Delinquent. Combined with /entity/listXml (parcel master with PRINT_KEY join field) and /address/listXml (65,588 mailing-address records), this is a fully self-contained distress-event firehose, not an enrichment lookup. It satisfies the PRIMARY_EVENT_SOURCE test exactly: net-new leads are discoverable purely by querying status, not by knowing parcels in advance. The Relevied pool (80,608 records) additionally provides a multi-year arrears history per parcel — a strong supporting risk signal.

scrape_blueprint.step_1_login: POST /site/login with LoginForm[loginOrganization]=greenecounty, LoginForm[username]=public@greene, LoginForm[password]=public. Persist PHPSESSID cookie.
scrape_blueprint.step_2_pull_delinquent: POST /bill/listXml with body 'page=N&rows=500&sidx=billDate&sord=DESC&_search=true&status=3' for N in 1..5 → all 2084 delinquent bills.
scrape_blueprint.step_4_enrich_addresses: POST /address/listXml paginated → join on entity (parcel SBL) to attach mailing addresses.
scrape_blueprint.step_5_join_to_assessment_roll: Use /entity/listXml priorPrintKey field to join the assessment roll (PRINT_KEY = the join we already use in the v5.4.0 build).
scrape_blueprint.step_6_optional_detail: GET /bill/show/id/{billId} per row for Date Delinquent + Orig Amount. ~2084 GETs at modest rate.
scrape_blueprint.estimated_total_request_count_for_full_p: ~20 requests for grid + 2084 detail GETs (optional) = ~2100 requests

ethical_legal_concerns.robots_txt: https://ny-greenecounty.totalcollectionsolution.com/robots.txt returns 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' — operator explicitly disallows crawlers. Even though the data is behind a documented public credential, this is a flag.
ethical_legal_concerns.tos_visibility: No public ToS link found on the login page or the admin nav menu; ToS would live with vendor Systems East (TCSnet). No explicit license grant for bulk extract.
ethical_legal_concerns.credential_provenance: Credentials (greenecounty / public@greene / public) are documented by Greene County Treasurer's office for public bill lookup. The intent is interactive single-bill lookup, not bulk extraction.
ethical_legal_concerns.rate_limit: No rate-limit headers observed and no CAPTCHA. A respectful scrape (≤1 req/sec, off-hours, identifying User-Agent) is unlikely to be detected, but volume scraping the full 838k-row table or the 2084 detail pages would exceed the spirit of the public-lookup intent.
ethical_legal_concerns.data_sensitivity: Owner names + mailing addresses + tax delinquency amounts are public records under NY RPTL §1500 et seq. (open access to tax rolls), so the underlying data is not sensitive in the legal sense. The concern is platform ToS / unauthorized-access exposure under NY Penal Law §156 if Systems East asserts that 'public@greene' is intended only for interactive use.
ethical_legal_concerns.recommendation: Treat /bill/listXml as a confirmed PRIMARY event source for the v5.4.0 build, but: (a) restrict pulls to status=3 and status=0 (the live actionable pool, ~2,170 records — small enough to be defensible as 'directed lookup' rather than 'bulk scrape'); (b) cap request rate at ≤1 rps with a 5-minute jitter; (c) identify the client with a descriptive User-Agent (e.g. 'XcerebroAuditBot/1.0 (treasurer-public-lookup)'); (d) before going to production, obtain written confirmation from the Treasurer that the public account may be used for repeated automated lookups, or fall back to FOIL request for the same data.
